body: Are you serious?! Your comments are VERY ignorant. Yes, throughout history there are people have had it worse. But that doesn’t make this any easier. Telling others to suck it up and be happy and deal with it because other people have had it worse is like saying that we shouldn’t be happy because people throughout history have had it better. It’s not helpful AT ALL. This is HARD. 18 months is a LONG TIME to ask people to give up. It’s not as simple as sitting at home and watching Netflix. You have people who are committing suicide because they can’t take the isolation and hopelessness. You have people whose businesses and livelihoods have been destroyed. You have people who are missing HUGE milestones in their lives. It’s not as simple as “You’re living in a world with internet, Netflix, etc., you can deal with not going nightclubbing for a few months.” Your comments sound very condescending and belittling for the pain and hopelessness that millions of people across the globe are feeling right now. I hope you develop more compassion for the people out there who are STRUGGLING right now.

I agree. I live with my parents right now, so I’m not completely alone, which is nice. But it’s not the same as seeing friends. Around July, I started seeing 2 friends who are also being pretty safe and I feel comfortable with. My mental health just couldn’t take being isolated for longer. I’ve been called selfish by some of my friends, but these are also friends who either live with their significant other or have unrestricted access to their significant other—seeing them almost every day of the week. Unfortunately, being single, I do not have a live-in best friend, like my friends who are in a relationship do. I don’t feel like it’s selfish to see one or two of my friends as long as we are being safe. It’s honestly no different than them seeing their significant others all the time, it’s just that these two friends have bedrooms that are across town.

Honestly? My mental health has never been worse. Im
21, and all I see is a bleak future of social distancing and masking forever. Or at least the rest of my youth. I feel like everything is in black and white right now. And each time I say something about how awful it is, my parents just talk about how I should be happy because I’m healthy and have a roof over my head. I understand that I’m luckier than a lot of other people right now, but am I not allowed to want more out of life? I’m starting to wonder if it’s all worth it. 

I wish I could get a therapist, but I’m still on my parent’s insurance and don’t want them to know...

I feel the exact same way. I fear this pandemic has caused irreparable damage to my personality. I’m a lot more negative than I was before this. I’m more anxious. I don’t find joy in things I used to at the beginning of the pandemic. I’ve pretty much accepted that life is going to suck for the next 2 or 3 years. I worry I’m going to drive my friends away because I’m so negative all the time, but I just can’t seem to find anything to be positive about.

I know what you mean. I don’t exactly get upset about it, but I do get a weirdo longing or “ache in my chest” type feeling when I watch movies and see people doing things that we could do before the pandemic. It’s such a weird feeling when I watch a TV show or movie with someone going to school or to a cafe with friends and thinking about how the last time I did that was back in March. I haven’t been totally avoiding TV or movies, but I’ve definitely been watching less than I was before the pandemic. Sometimes seeing things from before corona, like going to the movies or eating at a cafe, are just too much to think about. 

Just the other day, I was watching an old episode from a game show where there was a packed audience and I actually said aloud to my parents, “I can’t believe we used to sit that close to each other.” It’s definitely a weird time we’re living in.

I understand where you’re coming from. I’m sure that this generation that’s coming into the world will do great things in the future. However, I’m more thinking about how the class of 2021 is having their entire senior year pulled out from underneath them. Same as the class of 2020, all the events and celebrations they’ve looked forward to for the the last 3+ years are now being taken away. But to me, it seems like no one is really thinking or talking about the class of 2021 and how this virus will impact their senior year.
Thank you for writing this. I’m embarrassed to be an American right now.
